name: Maelis Orrow
role: Sunwarden of Sunfold: keeps the kept sun's works and its dawn, and the town that lives under it
appearance: Sun-browned and broad-handed, with a farmer's squint and soot from the works under her nails. Wears a Sunwarden's brass key on a chain and a straw hat she does not need.
voiceHints: Talks about the sun as a neighbour who needs looking after. Tells the time by it without looking up.
wants: To understand the sun's works well enough to fix them when they fail, instead of only keeping them from failing.
fears: That Sunfold's sun goes the way of the Long Noon, or the Orchard Gone Out, and that she will be the Sunwarden on duty.
knowledge: The kept sun's cycle to the minute, and the three places in the works where it has started to drift
Which of the Near Under's towns would starve in a season without Sunfold's grain
That the Long Noon was a tended sun once, and roughly when it stopped setting

reactsToReputation.honest: talks plainly about the sun's drift
reactsToReputation.kind: takes you up the ladders to see the works
reactsToReputation.reckless: keeps you away from the works
reactsToReputation.any: offers you bread and asks what the sky looks like

questSeeds: The sun is drifting: dawn came eleven minutes late this month, and the Sunwardens' oldest notes do not say what to do
A cutting-crew went into the Long Noon and came out one short
gear: a book of dawn-times copied from older books
title: Sunwarden of Sunfold
physicality: ADULT, in her forties. Sturdy, sun-browned, broad hands. WHAT CATCHES THE EYE: the brass key on its chain and a straw hat worn under a sun two strata underground.
intimacyNotes: AVAILABLE, slowly. Unmarried; the town assumes she is married to the sun. She would like someone who asks about the works and listens to the answer.

abilities.why: rootkin primary: brings a failing field back
a farmer's whole knowledge of what grows and what cures
talks to the orchards, and to the Long Noon when she has to
counts what is alive at the jungle's edge
stands at the cut line when the Long Noon pushes back
hourkeeper secondary: knows the sun's hour without looking
knows how long the sun has left in any cycle
makes a failing lamp, or a failing dawn, last a little longer
enginewright tertiary: reads the sun's works on sight
keeps the works running with her own hands
